paper.title_en: Constraint-Preserving Quantum Circuit Compilation for Graph Independent Sets via Persistent Occupancy Encoding
paper.abstract_en: Constraint-preserving mixers for graph independent sets repeatedly evaluate overlapping neighborhood conditions, increasing CX costs across ordered quantum optimization circuits. We propose a structure-aware compiler that reuses these conditions through persistent occupancy encoding. Exploiting mutual exclusion within true-twin classes, our reversible encoding stores class occupancy on the original data register across mixer operations and cost layers. Local mixers are synthesized using target compensation, blockwise parity queries, and coherent restoration; nonuniform cost phases are preserved by an exact coefficient transformation. We prove that the compiled circuit reproduces the original program's unitary action on the feasible subspace for any prescribed operation order and independent layer parameters, and establish exact separability of source-level caching costs under a fixed synthesis recipe. Across 134 evaluation programs and 72 independent confirmation programs, total CX counts fall by 22.61% and 19.87%, respectively, relative to the best of six reference implementations selected per program. Against a matched no-cache implementation, persistent encoding yields additional reductions of 4.10% and 9.13%.
